The '''1890–91 Scottish Football League''' was the first season of the [[Scottish Football League]]. It began on 16 August 1890 and concluded on 21 May 1891. The league was won jointly by [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] who ended the season with an equal number of points.

==Season overview==
[[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] ended the league season with an equal number of points so a play-off match was organised at [[Cathkin Park (1872–1903)|Cathkin Park]] in [[Glasgow]] on 21 May 1891 to determine the winner.<ref name="SFHA_Playoff">{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/playoffs.htm |title=Scottish Football League & Scottish Premier League - Play-offs and Test Matches 1891-date |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104021657/https://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/playoffs.htm |archive-date=4 November 2013 |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref> The game ended in a 2–2 draw so both clubs were declared champions.

On 30 September 1890 after playing four games in the league, [[Renton F.C.|Renton]] was suspended by the [[Scottish Football Association]] for professionalism, and the club was subsequently expelled from the league with their record expunged.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/expulsions.htm |title=Scottish Football League Expulsions 1890-1953 |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414220908/http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/expulsions.htm |archive-date=14 April 2015 |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref> [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]], [[Third Lanark A.C.|3rd LRV]] and [[Cowlairs F.C.|Cowlairs]] were docked four points each for fielding ineligible players.<ref name="SFHA_deductions">{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/pointdeductions.htm |title=Scottish Football League & Scottish Premier League - League point deductions and awards 1890-date |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414163346/http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/pointdeductions.htm |archive-date=14 April 2015 |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref> At the end of the season, the bottom three teams had to submit applications to rejoin the league for the next season along with other non-league clubs. [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]], [[Vale of Leven F.C.|Vale of Leven]] and [[Cowlairs F.C.|Cowlairs]] submitted applications along with non-league club [[Leith Athletic F.C.|Leith Athletic]]. In the election, Cowlairs lost their league position to Leith Athletic, with St Mirren and Vale of Leven being re-elected.<ref name="SFHA_elections">{{cite web |url=http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/reelections.htm |title=Scottish Football League - Re-elections 1891-1951 |publisher=Scottish Football Historical Archive |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414174453/http://scottish-football-historical-archive.com/reelections.htm |archive-date=14 April 2015 |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref>

==Clubs==
The inaugural season of the Scottish Football League was contested by 11 clubs. This was reduced to 10 clubs after four games when [[Renton F.C.|Renton]] was expelled from the league for professionalism.

==Championship play-off==
Rangers defeated [[Third Lanark A.C.|3rd Lanark RV]] 4–1 in their final league match on 9 May 1891<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fitbastats.com/rangers/game.php?gameid=80394 |title=Rangers 4 - 1 Third Lanark, Scottish League (09/05/1891) |publisher=Fitbastats.com |access-date=27 July 2019}}</ref> to move level with Dumbarton on 29 points, and a play-off was organised to determine which team would be crowned champions. However, the match finished as a draw and, with no more dates available for a further replay before the end of the season, it was decided that Dumbarton and Rangers would be declared joint champions.<ref>[https://thenorthsection.co.uk/on-this-day-1891 On This Day In Football History: 21 May 1891], Russell MdFadyen, The North Section, 21 May 2019</ref><ref>[https://www.scottishleaguehistory.com/p/season-189091-may-1891.html Thursday, 21 May 1891], Scottish League History </ref><ref>[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=O6REAAAAIBAJ&sjid=pLUMAAAAIBAJ&pg=6182%2C4943053 Football. {{!}} League Championship–Rangers v. Dumbarton.] The Glasgow Herald, 22 May 1891</ref>
